subject: Request: one-time batch credits for student scholarship computational project
messages:
From: Elena Soto <e.soto@midtown.edu>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Midtown DataLab <datalab@midtown.edu>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Request: one-time batch credits for student scholarship computational project

Hi Vivek,

I hope you are well — I'm reaching out from Midtown University's DataLab. We're running a winter scholarship for undergrad research where 12 students (paired into 6 teams) will run language-model-based analyses on a de-identified historical corpus. The program runs Jan 4–Mar 1.

We are hoping Redwood can support the cohort with a one-time grant of inference credits to complete their experiments (training/eval-style runs, mostly batch jobs). Attached is a short scholarship proposal and our IRB confirmation (both as PDFs).

High-level details:
- Number of student teams: 6
- Expected job pattern: batch jobs (no streaming), 3–6 experiments per team, estimated 600–800 tokens per request on average
- Sensitive data: corpus has been de-identified; IRB attached

Could you let us know what kind of credit support you might be able to provide and any required paperwork? We can also provide a short evaluation plan if helpful.

Thanks for considering — this program is small but will be used in course projects and a final public poster session.

Best,
Elena Soto
Assoc. Professor, Computational Humanities
Midtown University
[e.soto@midtown.edu]

[attachment: scholarship-proposal.pdf]
[attachment: IRB-approval-scan.pdf]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Prof. Elena Soto <e.soto@midtown.edu>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 13:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: one-time batch credits for student scholarship computational project

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear note and for sending the IRB. Really appreciate the program detail. I'm looping in Marissa (partnerships) and Ben (academic programs) to scope an appropriate package.

A few quick clarifying questions that will help us size credits:
1) Do you have an estimate of total model tokens or wall-time across the cohort (e.g., rough total inference hours or an upper bound)?
2) Which model family do you expect to use (smaller research model vs a larger LLM)? We can propose quantization/throughput options once we know.
3) Confirm that there is no PHI or PII in the dataset (IRB suggests de-identified, just want explicit confirmation).

If convenient, Marissa can propose a one-time pilot allocation and a requested evaluation checklist we use for academic grants (simple metrics + a short post-pilot write-up). Once we have those answers we can prepare a credit note and the minimal agreement.

I'll leave next steps to Marissa/Ben — thanks again and enjoy the rest of your weekend.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

[internal note: intake form may be required — see attachment template]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Prof. Elena Soto <e.soto@midtown.edu>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: one-time batch credits for student scholarship computational project

Hi Elena — great to meet you over email. Marissa here (partnerships). Thanks Vivek for the intro.

We can provision a provisional pilot allocation to support the scholarship cohort. Based on the estimates in your proposal, we can offer an initial 120k token-credit allocation (approx. 120 GPU-hours depending on model family) as a one-time grant for Jan–Mar. A few operational points before we finalize: 

- Confirmation of no PHI/PII in the dataset is required. Please reply explicitly.
- We ask for a one-page post-pilot summary from the lead instructor describing the experiments run and one representative result (this helps our academic program).
- We'll create a short credit agreement (one page) — attached is a stub for review.

If that's acceptable, we'll:
1) Create a HubSpot record (Deal DL-1123) and generate the credit allocation
2) Send the one-page agreement and intake form (for expected token budget, model family, and schedule)
3) Provision credits the week before your Jan 4 start date

Please confirm the PHI question and, if possible, provide a simple estimate of total expected requests (or an approximate total tokens).

Thanks — happy to fast-track this.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

[attachment: credit-agreement-stub.pdf]
[internal link: HubSpot DL-1123]

From: Elena Soto <e.soto@midtown.edu>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Midtown DataLab <datalab@midtown.edu>, student-coordinator@midtown.edu
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 10:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: one-time batch credits for student scholarship computational project

Marissa / Vivek — thank you, this is wonderful news and exactly the structure we were hoping for.

To confirm explicitly: the corpus has been de-identified and no PHI/PII will be processed. The IRB confirmation we attached covers the de-identification process; happy to share additional documentation if needed.

Estimated usage:
- Approx. 6 teams x 5 experiments x ~700 tokens avg = ~21,000 tokens per round; many experiments will be batched, but to be conservative we estimate a total of ~100k tokens for the full cohort across the term. If you prefer to size by wall-time, we expect short batch runs; let us know which metric works best for you.

Timeline:
- Jan 4: students begin
- Jan 18–Feb 8: main experiment window
- Feb 20–Mar 1: poster preparation and writeups

I've attached a simple run plan CSV with expected job cadence. Please let us know if the 120k token allocation looks acceptable and where we should sign the short agreement.

Thanks again to the team at Redwood — this support makes a big difference for a small program.

Warmly,
Elena Soto
Assoc. Professor, Computational Humanities
Midtown University

[attachment: run-plan.csv]
